F-nei7 — source-assisted image reading, 22 September 2026

This is a substantive assisted revision, not a second independent reading. It uses the preserved review-2026-09-22-image-only response, the preceding fragment report and its transcription, the cached Fragmentarium images, and the primary-text comparisons listed below. Reader: Codex subagent; exact model identifier unavailable. No human palaeographic review is claimed.

Image basis and references

The neutral image-001.png is the recto top band represented by r_band1.jpg. Recto line numbers count from the first text row on fol. [1]r; verso numbers restart at fol. [1]v. Full-side images r_1600.jpg and v_1600.jpg were inspected for layout and line location. Original-detail views of r_band1.jpg, r_band2.jpg, r_band4.jpg, r_band7.jpg, r_band8.jpg, v_band1.jpg, v_band2.jpg, and v_l5_zoom.jpg support the selections below. These are overlapping cached crops, not additional text. The cached crops are reduced derivatives; their precise native-image crop coordinates were not recovered. Image source: https://fragmentarium.ms/metadata/iiif/F-nei7/manifest.json, canvases labelled fol. [1]r and fol. [1]v.

Proposed expansions are in parentheses. Question marks retain uncertain readings, including some abbreviation expansions. [illegible] means that the present review does not resolve the visible group. Ellipses in square brackets identify intentionally untranscribed material. End-of-line hyphens represent word continuation and are editorial. Punctuation and u/v are lightly normalized. This is a selected, provisional transcription, not a complete diplomatic edition.

r.9 r(ati)o formalis amandi v(e)l op(er)andi, q(uia) e(ss)et eis r(ati)o e(xi)stendi?, sicut h(abe)t videri infra d. 32. Q(uod)?

The groups read e(xi)stendi? in r.8–9 have visible material beyond a simple e- abbreviation; the preceding report's essendi expansion is not silently adopted. Their precise expansion remains unsettled. The small word before aliquis is also uncertain. The initial image-only reading's quidem? (r.2) and unresolved ūbum groups are corrected to productum and verbum on this assisted image review. Its nō at r.1 is revised to tamen. The disputed end of r.4 and middle of r.5 remain tentative.

Corollary, r_band4.jpg

r.23 ati et creabilis, sicut visum est sup(ra) d. 18. Ex hiis p(ate)t correlarie q(uod)? emanat(i)o crea-
r.24 turar(um) [abbreviation unclear] a Deo n(e)c(essari)o p(re)supponit emanationem p(er)s(on)ar(um) divinar(um), et p(er) (con)s(equen)s ph(ilosoph)i q(ui) ema-
r.25 nat(i)o(n)em p(er)s(on)ar(um) divinar(um) ignoraveru(n)t, emanationes c(re)at(ur)ar(um)? a D(e)o no(n) b(e)n(e) intellexer(un)t
r.26 et i(de)o non e(st) miru(m) si c(irca) h(oc) multiplic(ite)r erraveru(n)t. Sic (er)g(o) p(ate)t ad obiectione(m) p(ri)mam, q(uod)

The sign between creaturarum and a Deo in r.24 remains unresolved; vel is not accepted merely because it appeared in the preceding report. The later connective is read per consequens, revising that report's propter quod. The common theological proposition in these lines is not by itself an author identifier.

The break vi- at r.39 is not completed from grammatical expectation. The nominatives relatio and proprietas at r.48 are retained as read rather than regularized. No deletion or added word is confidently identified in the selected recto passages.

Verso opening, v_1600.jpg and v_band1.jpg; reference number also checked in v_l5_zoom.jpg

v.1 p(er)sonalis s(ed) t(antu)m notio. Negatio e(n)i(m) sicut s(upra) d(i)c(tu)m est, maxime illa que dat intellig(er)e po(siti)onem,
v.2 bene p(otes)t notificare, sicut fuit exemplificatu(m) de ove non signata. Et ita sunt tres p(ro)p(ri)eta-
v.3 tes, s(cilicet) p(ate)rnitas, filiatio et p(ro)cessio, et 4(or) relationes, (con)numerata? cu(m) p(re)dictis trib(us) co(mmun)i spiratione
v.4 activa, et 5 notiones, (con)numerata? cu(m) p(re)dictis 4(or) innascibilitate, de quib(us) habebit(ur) infra
v.5 d. 26. Ex hiis et(iam) p(ate)t int(er) multas alias una r(ati)o dissimilitudinis int(er) innascibilitatem
v.10 Circa 2m p(ri)ncipale [illegible]

The count of properties, relations, and notions is legible, but the abbreviated connective participle in v.3–4 remains uncertain. These lines revise the earlier report's quia ille tres/quia ille: the image has a counting construction with cum predictis. The later worn lines v.6–9 are not newly transcribed. v.10 is underlined; only its opening is retained. The photographs do not determine whether the largely uninscribed remainder was erased or left blank, or why copying ends here.

Source comparisons actually checked

1. Richard of Middleton, Commentarius in Libros Sententiarum I, d.28, a.2, qq.1–2: https://reader.lombardpress.org/text/kzz7yh/kzz7yh-a61823 . Read as an online text transcription, not a checked print image. It compares innascibility's primary negative signification with secondary primacy and paternity/active spiration. This is a thematic and argumentative parallel to r.40–48, not sustained matching wording. No attribution or exclusion of Richard's entire corpus follows.
2. Thomas of Strasbourg, Commentarius in Libros Sententiarum III, d.11, q.1, a.1: https://reader.lombardpress.org/text/HuYgTa/HuYgTa-175910 . Read as online transcription, not a checked print image. It asks whether the production of creatures presupposes the emanation of the divine persons and distinguishes priority in order from causal priority. It supports the non-exclusive character of the subject in r.23–26, but does not reproduce the manuscript's sequence or the philosophers corollary as a sustained passage. No direct dependence is established.
3. Francis of Meyronnes, Venice 1520 collection: https://books.google.com/books?id=QJ4loltkxYEC . Cached OCR (meyr1520.txt) was inspected around the sequence marked question XV near the end of the Quodlibet and around the innascibility discussion. Heavy OCR loss and column mixing prevent a reliable passage comparison. SIEPM's linked Quodlibet image file and the Archive viewer could not be fetched with available access; a shell attempt failed at DNS. No print page was inspected. The prior report's exact column reference remains unverified, and Meyronnes remains unconfirmed, not excluded.
4. Web searches used the image-checked anchors about divine persons ignored by philosophers, innascibility/catholice/sustineri, and relegandum a divinis. No sustained candidate passage was retrieved. This is an unsuccessful retrieval outcome, not proof of unprinted status or an exclusion of named authors.

Result

Partial identification, low confidence: anonymous scholastic theological discussion, probably part of a commentary or question sequence on Sentences I. The Word/Love discussion, the reference to book II, and references to distinctions support that context. No author, exact distinction, edition identification, direct borrowing, date refinement, or novelty claim is established. Manuscript image review supports the selected readings above with explicit unresolved groups; edition comparison does not certify every word.
